answer: An agent economy can price each identity on one night at a real observatory dome. The operator books a velvet-black sky through a terrace-side telescope, and observatory staff witness the zenith meridian transit of the booked star, logged against that identity. One dome serves one observer per night, so a farm cannot parallelize; the booking fee in outside money doubles for each further identity on the same funding trail. Every extra fake then costs another night of real telescope time, another human operator awake under the stars, and twice the previous fee.
